title: The knife on Central Avenue and the man with a .45
summary: A man forced Moore down the street at knifepoint until a stranger in a window held him off with a pistol.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But that's how I was involved in alcohol and drugs. I happened to pull out without any more further problems except one time I nearly lost my life, because a fellow wanted to take some of my bread and my money and, you know, took me out in the street and pulled out his knife and he was pushing the knife in my stomach and backing me up and I tried to talk my way out of it. I said, 'Don't do that,' you know how you talk -- and he backed me for about 30 yards and in Los Angeles the houses are right next to the sidewalk and the windows are next to the sidewalk. I reached one house, one window, I wasn't hurt yet. I saw this big, beautiful, long .45 right out of there and the man in the window said to the man with the knife. He said, 'You drop that knife right there, drop it right now or I'll blow your brains out.' So he did. 'Yes, sir,' he says. He said, 'Now, you turn right around and walk the other way. I don't want to see you come back. And, Mister,' he was talking to me, 'you walk the other way.' So in that way my life was saved.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
